clips.title: The story
paras: A Task Unfinished is a simple delivery quest highlighting the strain young tauren endure during their coming-of-age rites on Red Cloud Mesa. Overburdened by the demands of their trials and a filial chore, an exhausted youth asks a passing traveler to carry a bundle of furs down to Innkeeper Kauth in Bloodhoof Village.

High upon Red Cloud Mesa, young tauren face rigorous trials of passage to prove their readiness for the wider world. Balancing traditional rites against ordinary tribal chores can push a youth to the brink of physical exhaustion. Faced with an unfinished Rite of Strength and an urgent chore from their father, one young tauren seeks the aid of a passing traveler to carry a bundle of furs down the mesa.

The destination for the furs is Bloodhoof Village, a welcoming haven resting in the open plains below. Innkeeper Kauth eagerly receives the delivery, intending to turn the pelt bundle into warm blankets for weary wanderers. The errand highlights both the hospitality of the plains tauren and the importance of rest, showing that community support underpins every solitary trial of strength.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Friend, please, I beg of you, can you help me? I have not finished my tasks here on the Mesa--I'm in the middle of my Rite of Strength--and my father asked me to deliver these furs to the inn in Bloodhoof.
I'm far from rested enough to complete both my rite and this task for my father. Would you mind going on for me?
The inn is pleasant and a perfect place to rest during your long travels. I'm sure you'll agree once you see it.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Yes, young one? What can Kauth do for you?
The journey here from the Mesa can be a tremendous burden for some, but a welcome sight for others. Which is it for you, I wonder?

clips.title: Completion
paras: Ah, the furs I was expecting. Thank you.
These came faster than I had expected. They will make good blankets for anyone who wishes to stay here.

Please feel free to stay as long as you like. My inn is always open and all of our people are welcome here. And don't underestimate a good night's rest, it can make a great difference while you're out traveling.
